question: Should crawl-remote deployments permanently retain this hidden Gitcrawl canary across rollbacks and require exact deployed-release provenance from every query envelope?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent, but code review cannot choose the permanent hosted-data and rollback contract or authorize the cross-repository production landing order.

options.title: Approve after staged proof
options.body: Accept the permanent canary contract and land the dependency stack after staged live deployment and rollback evidence confirms the documented invariants.

options.title: Require reversible canary lifecycle
options.body: Revise the design to remove or explicitly migrate canary state while preserving a proven rollback path before landing.

options.title: Pause the deployment gate
options.body: Keep the stack unmerged until maintainers choose a different production query-proof strategy.

recommendation.title: Approve after staged proof
recommendation.body: Accept the permanent canary contract and land the dependency stack after staged live deployment and rollback evidence confirms the documented invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the connected Gitcrawl evidence, deployment-canary, and downstream receipt stack and is best positioned to present the intended rollout and rollback contract for approval.
